title: A stage's traits (offered as a next step, read-only) are declared once on its template (tidy first, before LIN-4251)
description:
## Goal

A stage's traits are declared once, on its template: whether it is offered as a next step, and whether it is read-only. Everything that asks reads that one declaration: the stage selector, the router's refusal, the task page's "Another step" list and the dispatch preamble. Then changing a trait is a one-line edit to the template.

## Context

* LIN-4248 (`29f14bf6e`) added two hand-only, read-only stages. "Hand-only" is now a name list (`EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION`, `lib/prompt-templates.js`) beside the template's missing `route`. "Read-only" is a second name list (`SURVEY_KINDS`, `lib/proxy-preamble.js`), and the kind literals are copied in three test files.
* Two independent blind reads of that merge both scored it "mixed" for exactly this: it followed the per-kind pattern without reducing it.
* LIN-4251 is waiting to make four more stages read-only (look-into, context, retro, triage). Today that means extending a hand-kept list.

## This step

A tidy, done first as its own task, with **no behaviour change**: every kind's dispatched prompt stays byte-identical on every entry path. The traits live on the template definitions. The two name lists are derived from them or deleted, and the copied literals in tests read the traits. A template that doesn't declare its traits fails a test.

**Not this ticket:** changing what any stage is told (LIN-4251 does that next, on top of this); folding the other per-kind tables (leads, grounding, buckets, completion signals) into the template. Name in the report what folding those would take, without doing it.

## Done when

* Before and after, every kind's rendered dispatch prompt is byte-identical on every entry path, and the router's byte-pinned fixtures are unchanged.
* No hand-kept list of stage names remains for "offered" or "read-only".
* A missing trait fails a test.

## Report back

Where each trait now lives, who reads it, what was deleted, and what folding the remaining per-kind tables would take.

## At merge (who else must learn about it)

* The golden is byte-identical, and the router's `tests/fixtures/stage-router-prompts/` are unchanged.
* No hand-kept list of stage names remains for "offered" or "writes".
* The LIN-4248 preamble and dispatch-path tests have moved with the new parameter.
* Any doc that describes how a stage is kept out of routing or made read-only (e.g. `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md`) says the new thing.

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out.* Implemented as approved in [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2290](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2290>) (merge commit `d9c0f1caedd3506ef35c9ef0da6ab840d4ebb714`, deployed): `route` and `writes` are declared once on each template; the two name lists were derived or deleted; no deviations from the plan. The plan's sweep table, landing order, witnesses and the pre-work Survey guidance are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail. The folding report for the remaining per-kind tables is in the PR body and the close-out comment.

fits one session
plan-review due: no

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4253 @ 29f14bf6e

Read at `29f14bf6e` (the LIN-4248 merge), in a scratch worktree.

**Why this will be difficult**

1. **"Offered" is already declared twice.** The selector (`lib/prompt-templates.js:430`) reads `t.route && !EXCLUDED…`. The router's refusal (`lib/action-kind.js:18`) and "Another step" (`task-page-loader.js:1022` → `public/prompt-section.js:1341`) read only the Set. All three excluded kinds have no `route`, so the two agree, but only by coincidence. An `offered: false` flag next to an optional `route` would be a third declaration that can drift. My pick: an explicit `offered` boolean, plus a test that `offered ⇔ route present`.

2. **The preamble deliberately avoids importing the registry** (`lib/proxy-preamble.js:180-186`). Token, store and scope modules import it, so pulling in `prompt-template-defs.js` there risks import cycles. `lib/dispatch-entrance.js:66` already imports `PROMPT_TEMPLATES` and passes `kind: resolvedKind` (`:1083`). It should resolve the trait there and pass a boolean down. Kinds with no template (`'custom'` from collective, feedback triage) must default to false. The LIN-4248 dispatch-paths test checks `kind` at that wire, so it changes too.

3. **"Read-only" is two things, and a third copy already exists.** The Survey gate swaps both the mandate and a Survey-only closing ("only write is the one comment… end with the link"). LIN-4251 wants triage read-only, yet triage's lead says "These updates are yours to make". Separately, `STAGE_INTENT`'s `READING` (`lib/prompts/stage-intent.js`) is a hand-kept read-only list (context, look-into, retro, Surveys). The deeper gap is that nothing declares *what a stage may write*. A boolean `readOnly` will already be the wrong shape for LIN-4251. Name the trait after what it controls (e.g. `writes: 'one-comment'`), and report the overlap with `READING`.

4. **Nothing proves "byte-identical on every entry path" today.** There are router fixtures, the task-page golden, size budgets, and a three-path witness. The witness covers only the Surveys plus one control.

5. **Tests that derive from the trait are circular.** If tests read the trait under test, flipping it passes silently. Keep one test that pins the trait values, with its reason. Leave `completion-signals.test.js`'s kind lists alone; they belong to an out-of-scope table.

**What I'd do first**

Before refactoring, at `29f14bf6e`: commit a characterisation golden of every `PROMPT_TEMPLATES` kind. Render each through the three paths in `lin-4248-survey-dispatch-paths.test.js` (explicit `kind`, `promptName`-derived, recommend-and-dispatch override), plus `generatePrompt` and `formatStageOptions()`. Then refactor against that golden. The derived `excluded` array keeps the order retro, survey-task, survey-place (template insertion order), which `lin-3833-another-step-fit.test.js:21` pins.

**Folding the other tables** (report only)

`STAGE_LEADS` and `COMPLETION_SIGNALS` are already keyed lookups inside the defs, so folding them is mechanical. Grounding (`prompt-formatters.js:616`), run-view labels, wall-clock buckets, `llm-jobs` and `STAGE_INTENT` live in leaf modules so their readers avoid the registry. Folding them hits the same import-direction problem as #2. The options are callers that resolve the value and pass it down, or a dependency-free trait table that the defs spread in.

## Survey global: LIN-4253 @ 29f14bf6e

**Where it lands.** `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` (19 templates), `lib/prompt-templates.js` (`EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION`, `getSelectableStages`), `lib/action-kind.js` (router refusal), `lib/task-page-loader.js:1022` → `public/prompt-section.js:1341` (`summary.excluded`), and `lib/proxy-preamble.js` (`SURVEY_KINDS`, gated at `:260`, fed `resolvedKind` from `lib/dispatch-entrance.js:1083`). This part is mostly getting better: the selector already reads its options off each template's `route` (LIN-3300), and completeness tests already pin per-kind tables to `PROMPT_TEMPLATES` keys (`STAGE_LEADS`, `STAGE_INTENT`, `BUCKET_OF_KIND`, grounding). LIN-4248 was the first change in a while to add hand-kept name lists rather than reduce them.

**The redundancy is already exact.** The three templates with no `route` (retro, survey-task, survey-place) are exactly the three in `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION`. So "offered" is already declared once, by whether `route` is there; the Set just says it a second time. The obvious way to do it, adding `offered: false` next to a missing `route`, would leave two signals for one fact on every template. Better: make `route` an own property on every template (`route: null` for hand-only ones), derive "excluded" from that, and have the test check `Object.hasOwn(t, 'route')`. `rejectExcludedKind` has to ask `PROMPT_TEMPLATES[kind]?.route === null`, not `!route`, because meta kinds like `defer` have no template and must stay allowed. `summary.excluded` can stay as a derived array, so the client doesn't change. The prose "Hand-triggered only, never routed" in the two Survey `description`s says it a third time. It isn't dispatched, so it can stay.

**Read-only has a placement problem.** `proxy-preamble.js` says on purpose that it doesn't import the template registry. Importing it now would break that and pull the whole defs graph into a low-level module. The cleaner seam: `dispatch-entrance` resolves `PROMPT_TEMPLATES[resolvedKind]?.readOnly === true` and passes a boolean (`readOnly`), and the preamble stops knowing about kinds. That changes the `attachProxyContext` / `buildProxyContextPreamble` parameter, so `lin-4248-survey-preamble.test.js` and `lin-4248-survey-dispatch-paths.test.js` have to move with it. Keep their literal copies of the *sentences* (they guard drift). Only the literal copies of *kinds* should go.

**"Read-only" already lives in two more places, informally.** `STAGE_INTENT` gives `READING` to context, look-into, retro and the surveys. `GROUNDING_BY_KIND` gives `[STALE]` / `[]` with a "read-only or look-back" rationale. LIN-4251's set (look-into, context, retro, triage) nearly matches the first. A new `readOnly` trait will sit next to both without explaining how it relates. At minimum, add a test or comment saying whether `readOnly ⇒ READING`. Don't fold them.

**Byte-identity.** `getSelectableStages` iterates `Object.entries`, so key order and the `tests/fixtures/stage-router-prompts/` pins survive as long as no template is reordered. Adding properties to template objects changes no rendered text. The other code that iterates templates (`audit.js:586`, `task-mode-store.js`) reads only named fields or keys, so new properties don't leak.

**Better still, not this task.** One `traits`/`kind` descriptor per template, carrying lead, intent, grounding, bucket, completion signals and run-view label (`run-view.js:73`, `llm-jobs.js:54`). Today each of those is a keyed table with its own completeness test. Folding them is mechanical but touches every stage's rendered prompt path. Their completeness tests become shape tests, and `wall-clock-summary`'s meta kinds (`autopilot`, `wake`, `custom`) still need a table of their own.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve: the premise checks out against `29f14bf6e` (still `origin/main`, nothing landed on the touched files since the ticket), and built as written the plan delivers all three Done-when items with no behaviour change.

**What I checked, at HEAD**

- **Offered = `route`.** Live registry: 19 templates. Exactly `retro`, `survey-task` and `survey-place` lack an own `route`, and `[...EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION]` is `['retro','survey-task','survey-place']`, which is template insertion order. So deriving the Set from `route === null` gives the same membership and the same order (`lin-3833-another-step-fit.test.js:21`). The `.has('x')` check at `:43` still works because the export stays a Set. `getSelectableStages` (`prompt-templates.js:430`) filters on `t.route`, and `null` is falsy, so router fixtures can't move. `rejectExcludedKind` using `PROMPT_TEMPLATES[kind]?.route === null` keeps `defer` and `custom` allowed (no template, so `undefined`). Prototype names like `constructor` give `undefined` too.
- **Nothing leaks from the new properties.** Every other `template.route` reader (`render-prompts.js:26`, `audit.js:598`, `scripts/audit-prompts.js:103,157`, `scripts/eval/jev-spike.mjs:58`) treats null and absent the same. No code spreads a template object or serializes it whole. Iterators read named fields or keys only (`prompt-templates.js:204,287,378`, `task-mode-store.js:68`, `audit.js:586`).
- **The preamble seam.** All lanes share it: the session lane `enterSessionDispatch`, the proxy lane, and recommend-and-dispatch all reach `dispatch-factory.js:1110` → `finalizePrompt(harness, effectiveKind)` → `dispatch-entrance.js:1083`. So resolving `writes` there covers every launch. The other `attachProxyContext` callers (`routes/collective.js:373`, `routes/workspace-api-feedback.js:266,329`, `proxy-preamble.js:808,834`) pass no `kind` today and will pass no `writes`, so they keep the default block.
- **Sweep.** I re-ran both greps. The hits outside the plan's table are vocabulary or prose, not trait lists: `lib/proxy-instructions.js:849` (the VERB OVERRIDE kind list), `public/llms.txt:269-270` (descriptions), `docs/prompt-pipeline/stage-descriptions/retro-audit.md:124` (a dated audit, already stale at `new Set(['retro'])`), the change log and the eval fixtures. None of them needs to move.
- **The "trap".** I confirmed it. `STAGE_INTENT` gives `READING` to context, look-into, retro and both Surveys (`lib/prompts/stage-intent.js`). Only the Surveys get the read-only preamble today. Declaring `'work'` on the other three is correct for this ticket.

**Notes for the builder** (none blocks)

1. **The prompt-size budget will go red at step 2. Plan for it.** `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` is 106888 bytes, exactly its ceiling in `tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js:72`, with zero headroom. Nineteen `writes:` lines, three `route: null` and an import will exceed it. Two ways through. Either raise that ceiling and `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES` by the measured delta, with the reason beside it (code, not prompt text; `LIN-3612`'s line at `:73` is the precedent). Or pay for the bytes by lowering the `lib/prompt-templates.js` ceiling (`:73`, 19970 against 19234 actual, and the hand-kept Set and its comment leave that file) so the total stays flat. Shorter rewording of the comments at defs `108-109` and `1167` also helps. Keep the declaration terse (for example `writes: W.WORK`).
2. **Widen the golden to the arms the three paths don't reach.**
   - The **claude-code / MCP** branch: the mandate sentence sits in both exchange branches (`proxy-preamble.js:352` and `:361`). The paths in `lin-4248-survey-dispatch-paths.test.js` resolve to prose unless a harness is set; `buildApp`'s `workspaceHarnessDefault` gives you that arm.
   - A **follow-up** (`followUpTo`): `provisionResumeCredential`'s attach (`proxy-preamble.js:808,834`) passes no `kind` today, so a Survey follow-up gets the default block.
   Keep that exactly as it is here. Threading `writes` into the resume would change output, so if it looks like a bug, name it for LIN-4251 rather than fixing it in this PR.
3. **Fail before the mint, not after.** In `attachProxyContext` the bootstrap is minted (around `:690`) before `buildProxyContextPreamble` runs (`:708`). If the unknown-value throw lives only in the builder, a bad value spends a token before it refuses. Validate `writes` at the top of `attachProxyContext` as well, or instead, so the refusal spends nothing (the same order LIN-4016's target refusal keeps in `dispatch-entrance.js:1027`).
4. **Bookkeeping that review will look for:**
   - A row in `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md`. `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md:34` says every template change gets one; this one is "no rendered change", direction recorded before merge.
   - A one-line entry for `lib/stage-writes.js` in `docs/architecture/source-map.md`, next to the other leaf modules that exist to avoid the registry (for example the `ownerless-token-policy.js` line).
5. **Removing the golden at step 5 is fine.** Name the commit where it ran green in the report, as the plan says. Commit 1's two red runs (a lead byte, a closing byte) are the evidence that the golden works, so keep their output in the report as well.

Session fit: one session, as the plan says.

**Tests and budget.** New `lin-4253-stage-traits.test.js` (completeness plus a non-circular pin table). The three LIN-4248 test files read kinds from the templates. Budget: defs +606 (code), prompt-templates −611, frozen total −5, reasons recorded.

## Review — LIN-4253

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2290 at head `85d7199d` (base `40557e9f`, still `origin/main`; nothing has landed on the touched files since the ticket was created).

CI: green on `85d7199d`. Run 42012805134: ci-success, Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4 and Secret scan (source) all pass.

**Scope against the plan.** The diff matches the plan's sweep table: 14 files, all within the planned places plus the two bookkeeping items plan-review asked for (the change-log row and the `source-map.md` line). The router fixtures (`tests/fixtures/stage-router-prompts/`) and `render-task-page-golden.json` are not touched. I re-ran the sweep greps at head. No hand-kept name list is left for "offered" or "writes". `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION` is derived from `route === null`. `SURVEY_KINDS` is gone from lib; the dispatch-paths test now has a local derived copy. `rejectExcludedKind` uses `?.route === null`. The preamble imports only `lib/stage-writes.js`, never the registry. All four other `attachProxyContext` callers (`routes/collective.js`, `routes/workspace-api-feedback.js` ×2, and the resume helper ×2) passed no `kind` before and pass no `writes` now, so they get the default block on both sides of the change.

**Independent byte-identity check (my own run, not the author's numbers).** I took the scaffold golden test from `93392209` and regenerated its fixture at base `40557e9f` myself. The result was identical to the committed fixture. I then ran the test against final head `85d7199d`: it passed, 1/1, with zero keys moved. That covers all 19 kinds × (`generatePrompt`, explicit `kind`, `promptName`-derived, recommend-and-dispatch, the claude-code MCP arm), plus the resume plain attach on both harnesses, `formatStageOptions`, the selectable keys, the excluded order and the refusals.

**Mutation checks (LIN-2274).** These ran against the six affected test files (129 tests, all green at baseline). Every mutation turned the suite red, and each was reverted afterwards:
- M1, `dispatch-entrance` passes `writes: undefined`: 6 fail (both Surveys on all three dispatch paths).
- M2, refusal `== null` (catches undefined too): 5 fail (`defer` and `custom` are refused).
- M3, `writes` dropped on survey-place: 3 fail (completeness, pin, preamble threading).
- M4, survey-task flipped to `W.WORK`: 1 fail (the pin table). This shows the non-circular check works.
- M5, `attachProxyContext` pre-mint validation removed: 1 fail ("refuses before it mints").
- M6, `route: null` dropped on retro: 5 fail (pin, excluded order, LIN-3833 Another-step).
- M7, one byte changed in the one-comment closing: 7 fail (the literal sentence pins).

**Regression check.** `git log` on the modified lib files shows LIN-4248 (`29f14bf6`) as the only recent change to this behaviour. Its read-only block is preserved byte for byte (M7 and the golden). Nothing reverted is re-applied.

**Gap analysis.** Every Done-when and At-merge item is addressed. Plan-review's notes 1–5 were all followed: the budget was paid net −5, the golden was widened to the MCP and resume arms, validation happens before the mint, the bookkeeping rows were added, and the golden was removed with its evidence named. The relation of `writes` to `STAGE_INTENT`/grounding is pinned by a test (`writes ≠ work ⇒ READING`, and the converse is false today) and explained in a comment in `stage-writes.js`. The folding report is in the PR body.

**One of a class?** The class is "a per-kind trait kept as a hand list outside the template". This ticket bounds two instances (offered, writes), and both are done. The other per-kind tables (`STAGE_INTENT`, `GROUNDING_BY_KIND`, buckets, run-view, llm-jobs, completion signals) are excluded by name and reported, not folded, which is correct. No sibling list for these two traits is left.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Byte-identity at the final head**, inside (Done-when 1). CI has no golden because the scaffold was removed. Discharged: I regenerated the golden at base myself and it passed at `85d7199d` (above).
- **Survey follow-ups (`followUpTo` → `provisionResumeCredential`) still get the default "open PRs" block**, outside. This existed before the change and is unchanged here by design, since byte-identity required it. It belongs to LIN-4251's class (which stages get which write mode), not this ticket. Close-out: add a comment to LIN-4251 saying (a) `SURVEY_KINDS` is gone and a stage's mode is now its template's `writes` (`lib/stage-writes.js`), so LIN-4251's "Work" paragraph is stale, and (b) the resume attach (`lib/proxy-preamble.js` `provisionResumeCredential`, both `attachProxyContext` calls) passes no `writes`, so a follow-up to any one-comment stage gets the work block. Check that LIN-4251 doesn't already say this before adding it.

Nothing else is outstanding. The e2e suite, unit tests and the router fixtures are covered by CI on the exact head.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The work is complete and matches the plan. I verified no behaviour change on my own, and the load-bearing tests fail when their code is mutated. The only open item is the outside-scope note to LIN-4251 described above.

## Close-out — LIN-4253

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2290, squash, pinned with `--match-head-commit 85d7199d` (the commit CI passed on). Merge commit `d9c0f1caedd3506ef35c9ef0da6ab840d4ebb714`. Review verdict was Approve, conditional on the close-out discharging the ledger.

**Changes I made at close-out:** none to code. Review asked for no code fixes, and the PR was clean and mergeable, so there was no conflict to resolve and nothing changed after approval.

**CI:** CI exists (`.github/workflows/test.yml`). Green on the exact head `85d7199d` before merge (run 42012805134: ci-success, Unit tests, E2E 1-4/4, Secret scan). Post-merge run on `main` (42014815693) for `d9c0f1ca`: success.

**Deploy:** GitHub deployment for `d9c0f1ca` (environment `linear-viewer`) reached `success`. Verified on the landed commit by reading its source: `SURVEY_KINDS` is gone from `lib/proxy-preamble.js`, which imports only `lib/stage-writes.js` (not the registry); `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION` in `lib/prompt-templates.js` is derived from `route === null`; `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` has 19 `writes:` declarations and 3 `route: null`. Byte-identity itself was proved before merge by review's independent golden run (see ledger); the golden is deliberately removed, so it cannot be re-run on the deployed commit.

**Ledger (from review's "What CI Did Not Prove"):**
- *Byte-identity at the final head* (inside): already discharged by review. Review regenerated the scaffold golden (`93392209`) at base `40557e9f` itself and it passed at `85d7199d`, 1/1, zero keys moved, across 19 kinds x all dispatch paths, the MCP arm, resume attach, `formatStageOptions` and the refusals. Plus seven mutation checks M1-M7, each turned the suite red. I did not re-run these; I am relying on that recorded evidence.
- *Survey follow-ups still get the default "open PRs" block* (outside): LIN-4251 did not yet record it, so I added a comment there (comment `2cdacc52`) saying `SURVEY_KINDS` is gone and a stage's mode is its template's `writes` (`lib/stage-writes.js`), and that `provisionResumeCredential` passes no `writes`. LIN-4251 is the right home (it is the ticket that decides which stages get which write mode), so no new ticket was filed. Linked the two as `related`.

**Post-deploy steps:** none were required by the ticket or the review. No post-deploy check was left unrun.

**Report back (from the PR body, kept here for the record):** `route` (offered, or `null` = hand-only) and `writes` (`work` | `one-comment`) now live on each template in `lib/prompt-template-defs.js`; the selector, router refusal, "Another step" list, dispatch-entrance and the preamble read them. Deleted: the hand-kept `SURVEY_KINDS` and the hand-kept excluded-name list. Folding the other per-kind tables: `STAGE_LEADS` and `COMPLETION_SIGNALS` are mechanical; `STAGE_INTENT`, `GROUNDING_BY_KIND`, wall-clock buckets, run-view labels and `llm-jobs` are read by registry-avoiding leaf modules, so either callers resolve from the template and pass values down, or a dependency-free trait table (the shape of `lib/stage-writes.js`) is spread into the defs; the meta kinds (`autopilot`, `wake`, `custom`) would still need their own table.

**Description:** archived to snapshots, then the implementation plan and Survey guidance pruned to a stub (full text is in the task snapshots and the comment trail).

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was this difficult?** It mostly wasn't. The design was settled before I started, and the code matched the plan. It bound in three places:
- **The preamble's import direction.** That is why `writes` is resolved in `dispatch-entrance` and handed down.
- **The prompt-size budget.** `prompt-template-defs.js` sat at its exact ceiling, so 19 one-line declarations needed a recorded raise. I paid for it with bytes freed in `prompt-templates.js`, and I shortened the declarations to `writes: W.WORK`.
- **The golden harness.** The real friction was here, not in the refactor. It was non-deterministic: the ephemeral test port leaks into the prompt's base URL. Its "prose" arm was also secretly the claude-code arm, because the default harness resolves there. Both would have made a green golden meaningless.

**2. What I would have done first.** What I did: the golden at base, with a determinism check before trusting it.

**3. What I would tidy.**
- `attachProxyContext` silently ignores a stale `kind:` argument. An unknown-parameter guard would turn a missed caller into an error.
- The `W` alias exists only to save bytes, and it reads cryptic.
- `SURVEY_READ_ONLY_MANDATE` keeps its Survey name inside a table keyed by `one-comment`.
- The follow-up resume path never threads `writes`, so a Survey follow-up gets the default block. Unchanged, but LIN-4251 should know.

**4. How this ticket would have looked if the area were how I'd want it.** One descriptor per template, with traits that leaf modules can read without importing the registry. A budget that counts rendered prompt text, not code bytes in the defs file. Then this ticket is a one-line template edit.

**5. What the ticket or plan got wrong.**
- It said the three dispatch paths in the LIN-4248 test were a usable base. They need a pinned harness and a pinned origin before they characterise anything.
- It said absent `writes` is `undefined`. `null` needs the same treatment.
- Removing the golden at the end leaves the byte-identity claim unreproducible after merge. The evidence lives only in the PR text, a trade the plan made without saying so.

**6. What the change left behind.**
- **Simpler:** the excluded set is derived, the selector filter is one clause, the preamble knows no stage names, and the test kind lists are gone.
- **New, with a home:** `lib/stage-writes.js`, listed in the source map.
- **In two places, deliberately:** the closing sentences, in `WRITES_BLOCK` and pinned literally in the test.
- **Did not learn about it:** `lib/proxy-instructions.js` (the VERB OVERRIDE kind list), `public/llms.txt`, and the stale retro-audit doc. The budget test also now carries a code-only raise, which muddies what its ceilings mean.

**7. Did the larger scope pay for itself?** Mostly yes, and cheaply. Most of the extra was proof, not code. The golden and the pin table paid for themselves. Without the golden, "byte-identical" would be an assertion. The pin table is the only check that fails if a trait flips. The docs bookkeeping was about a quarter of the effort and saved nothing here; it is for the next reader. I would have drawn the line at the same place for code. I would have kept the golden as a lasting test with a stable, rendered-text fixture, rather than building it and then deleting it.
